clue.text: Cry, given report of Trump's barrier?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so these words point to a word said aloud

parts.note: Donald Trump's promised border barrier with Mexico was a wall

explanation.surface: A protest shout prompted by news of the former US president's border project.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoken word for the barrier is entered as a word that sounds the same: a waul is a cat's wail.
explanation.definitionFit: To waul (or wawl) is to wail or howl like a cat, so it is a synonym of cry.

clue.text: Go towards a silvery fish, keeping very quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: the roach is a silvery freshwater fish
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: An angler's instruction: creep up silently on a gleaming fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' has the fish phrase hold the musical marking, which lands just after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach is to move nearer to something, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Minister is tense, having got nothing right

parts.note: the past is a grammatical tense
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A government minister on edge after achieving nothing correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests a politician, but it is the church sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor ministers to a congregation, so he or she is a minister of religion.

clue.text: This plant may be poisonous — peril I knew about

indicators.note: about here means turned around or scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning about a toxic plant from someone who already knew the danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges PERIL I KNEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Periwinkle (Vinca) is a trailing garden plant whose alkaloids make it toxic if eaten.

clue.text: Spoke angrily, being broke?

definitions.meaning: to speak sharply and irritably in a sudden outburst
to have broken in two, cracked suddenly

explanation.surface: Someone lost their temper; was it because they had no money?
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' hints at being penniless, but it is the past tense of break.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking curtly in anger and breaking with a crack are both senses of the same verb.

clue.text: Old-fashioned secretary taking various notes

indicators.note: various suggests differing arrangements, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A secretary of the old school jotting down assorted memos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges NOTES.
explanation.definitionFit: A steno, short for stenographer, took dictation in shorthand, a dated office role.

clue.text: Tidiest garden reconfigured and broken into smaller units

indicators.note: reconfigured means set out in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A neat garden that has been redesigned and split into plots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconfigured' rearranges TIDIEST GARDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has fallen apart into fragments is said to have disintegrated.

clue.text: Declares a piece of poetry 'inadequate'

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a verse is a stanza or piece of poetry

explanation.surface: A critic pronounces a poem not good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' cuts the final E from VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly, a synonym of declare.

clue.text: Choral music's central character, eccentric university type?

indicators.note: the central character of a word is its middle letter
eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Choral music sung by an oddball academic.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of MUSIC, S, joins CHORAL, and 'eccentric' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person, typically found at a university.

clue.text: Man who may be a lumberjack?

definitions.meaning: informally a man is a fella, also spelt with -er

explanation.surface: Describing a chap who might work cutting timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal word for a bloke is also literally one who fells trees.

clue.text: One day, having got tiddly, refused to budge

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday
tiddly and tight are both British slang for slightly drunk

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy one day who would not move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tiddly' is British slang for tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit tight is an idiom for staying put and not giving way.

clue.text: One to grumble about order more clearly expressed?

parts.note: c (circa) is Latin for about
the OM, Order of Merit, is a British honour
plainer means more clearly put

explanation.surface: A grouch moaning about instructions that should be clearer.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who grumbles habitually is a complainer.

clue.text: Job of female leading one church organisation to facilitate communication

parts.note: a post is a job
I is the Roman numeral one
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A woman's job heading a church body that helps people talk.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A post office handles letters and parcels, an organisation for sending messages.

clue.text: Ailments needing tablets, relieving the head

indicators.note: relieving means taking away, here from the front of the word

parts.note: pills are tablets

explanation.surface: Illnesses that require medication to ease a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relieving the head' removes the P from PILLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ills are ailments, a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: One creating trouble is meek if charm is found out

indicators.note: found out suggests something exposed in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A troublemaker hides behind meekness until their charm is exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found out' rearranges MEEK IF CHARM IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stirs up trouble is a troublemaker, the same idea.

clue.text: Piece on US gangster's virility

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts
hood, short for hoodlum, is American slang for a gangster

explanation.surface: A US mobster's gun ('piece') as a symbol of masculinity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' suggests a gun but is a game piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Manhood means masculinity, the qualities of an adult male.

clue.text: Wild mammals? Just pussies, as you might say

indicators.note: speaking the words points to a word that sounds alike

parts.note: mere means just or only, and pussies are cats

explanation.surface: Dismissing wild animals as nothing more than kittens.
explanation.definitionFit: Meerkats are small African mammals of the mongoose family living wild.

clue.text: What's only partially found, ocean wreck

indicators.note: only part of the words is shown, so the letters lie inside them

explanation.surface: A shipwreck only partly discovered on the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only partially found' marks letters spanning FOUND OCEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo is to ruin or destroy, so it can mean wreck.

clue.text: What's 'common' with beastly connotation?

parts.note: think of the phrase common sense, with an animal replacing the first word

explanation.walkthrough: Common sense with an animal twist gives the equine version.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse sense means practical good judgement, the same as common sense.

clue.text: Cheer from unruly yahoo outside front of restaurant

indicators.note: outside means the other letters go around
unruly means disorderly, so the letters are rearranged
the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rowdy lout shouting outside a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges YAHOO into HOOAY, which goes 'outside' the R from 'front of restaurant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooray is a shout of joy, a cheer.

clue.text: Pleasing little stone shelters

indicators.note: shelters means covers or holds, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A small charming rock providing cover.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sweet is pleasing or charming.

clue.text: Oppose criminal boldness

parts.note: con is short for convict, a criminal
front means nerve or effrontery

explanation.surface: Standing against a criminal's audacity.
explanation.definitionFit: To confront is to face up to and challenge, close to oppose.

clue.text: Shelter any number repeatedly in part of boat

indicators.note: in tells us to put the letters inside the other piece

parts.note: the keel runs along a boat's bottom

indicators.note: repeatedly means taken more than once, here twice

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Taking cover several times in a section of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles N to NN.
explanation.definitionFit: A kennel is a shelter for a dog.

clue.text: Limited number operating for a time

parts.note: limited here means shortened, and no is the abbreviation for number
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: A restricted group running for a set period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limited' signals the shortened form of number.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is midday, a particular time of day.

clue.text: What a surprise, baddy has gone round country house!

indicators.note: turning round means read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a baddy
ha is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: An exclamation as the villain is seen circling a mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has gone round' turns the villain backwards; the exclamation comes first in the clue but last in the answer. A cad is an old-fashioned British word for a bounder.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house or villa.

clue.text: Detective briefly restricts terrible riot in US city

indicators.note: restricts means confines, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: Det is the short form of detective

indicators.note: terrible means awful, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A policeman curbs a dreadful disturbance in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges RIOT into TROI, which DET 'restricts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is a city in Michigan, the home of the US car industry.
